fine_trace.code: md_html(data, size, process_output, NULL, parser_flags, renderer_flags);
fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled bytes (after 8-byte flags header) are passed as the Markdown input to md_html(), which forwards them to md_parse().
The raw input buffer and its size are handed to md_parse() for block/inline analysis.
md_parse() initializes MD_CTX with ctx.text=input and ctx.size=size, then invokes md_process_doc() which drives line analysis.
Each line is analyzed; when a '<' is encountered and HTML spans are enabled, md_analyze_line() calls md_is_html_any() to recognize inline raw HTML.

fine_trace.code: is_html = md_is_html_any(ctx, line, n_lines - line_index, off, lines[n_lines-1].end, &html_end);
fine_trace.note: md_is_html_any() is invoked with the current line pointer and remaining line count; it dispatches to md_is_html_comment()/md_is_html_declaration()/etc.
One of the HTML recognition helpers is selected based on the bytes following '<'; each helper calls md_scan_for_html_closer() to find the closing sequence.

The inner loop scans for the closing string. The loop guard is 'off + len <= lines[line_index].end && off + len <= max_end', but when the closing sequence spans a line boundary or the line end is at the buffer edge, md_ascii_eq() (memcmp) reads len bytes starting at off, which can read one byte past the allocated input buffer, causing the heap-buffer-overflow READ 1.
